bug_info.bug_desc: In host mode, the FSM did not properly distinguish a first START from a repeated START. The old no_stop/restart logic treated any START after a previous logged start as a restart, but the Active state always released SCL immediately when fmt_flag_start_before_i was set and went directly to SetupStart. For a repeated START, this skipped the normal ClockLow low phase, so SCL was released from the previous ACK/bit low state before the programmed low time had elapsed, producing a short SCL low pulse and a setup/timing violation before the repeated START. The fix introduces trans_started to know whether a transaction has already started, and a registered pending-restart request (req_restart/pend_restart) so that a restart can first go through the normal ClockLow period and only then enter SetupStart. The command-complete event was also updated to be emitted from log_start && pend_restart so it correctly marks the repeated START boundary instead of using the old combinational restart/no_stop condition.
bug_info.fix_hint: Replace no_stop/restart with trans_started and a registered pending-restart request. In Active, when fmt_flag_start_before_i is set but trans_started is true, keep SCL low, assert req_restart, and enter ClockLow instead of SetupStart. After the ClockLow period has elapsed, use pend_restart to branch to SetupStart for the repeated START; otherwise continue to ClockPulse. Clear pend_restart when the START is logged, clear trans_started on STOP or host disable, and assert event_cmd_complete_o only from log_start && pend_restart.
